topPRs.title: feat(op-service/clock): make AdvancingClock continuous
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Replaces the tick-pumped `AdvancingClock` (a `DeterministicClock` advanced by a fixed wall-clock ticker) with a lazy implementation:

- `Now()` = `wallClock.Now() + offset`, with no tick quantisation. Wall time progresses continuously and `AdvanceTime` jumps are visible immediately.
- A single scheduler goroutine sleeps until the next due action and fires everything overdue when woken. `AdvanceTime` signals the scheduler so jumped-past timers fire without waiting.
- `Timer`, `Ticker`, `After`, `AfterFunc`, and `SleepCtx` honour both wall progression and manual jumps. Stop/Reset semantics match the stdlib `time` package — including `Ticker.Reset(d)` updating the period and `AfterFunc` running its callback in its own goroutine.

All callers drop the now-unused `advanceEvery` argument from `NewAdvancingClock`.

While this is more code than the old version which reused DeterministicClock implementations, it is much more realistic so is better suited to being used to enable time travelling sequencers.

topPRs.title: feat(op-supernode): add top-level --dependency-set flag
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
The dependency set is a global property shared by every chain a supernode manages, but it was previously only reachable via the per-VN `--interop.dependency-set` flag inherited from op-node. Add a supernode-level `--dependency-set` flag (env `OP_SUPERNODE_DEPENDENCY_SET`), load it once, and override each virtual node config's `DependencySet`. The per-VN flag is added to `SupernodeOwnedFlags` so setting it logs a warning.

Closes ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#96

topPRs.title: chore(interopgen): move depset package to op-chain-ops/interopgen/config
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Relocates `op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/depset` to `op-chain-ops/interopgen/config` and renames the Go package from `depset` to `config`. The package is a set of config value types (`FullConfigSet`, `StaticRollupConfigSet`, `DependencySet`, `StaticConfigDependency`, `LinkChecker`, …) — its non-supervisor consumers are `op-chain-ops/interopgen`, `op-devstack/sysgo`, and `op-program`.

Step toward deleting op-supervisor: removes one of the remaining reasons it has to exist as a Go module dependency. No logic changes — pure relocation, with import paths and qualifiers rewritten across both external consumers and op-supervisor's own files. Files that also import `op-supervisor/config` use the alias `interopcfg` to avoid the package-name collision.

Also adds `op-chain-ops/interopgen/config/` to op-program's `Dockerfile.vmcompat.dockerignore` and `Dockerfile.repro.dockerignore` so the vm-compat analysis can still build `op-program/client` after the move. The package's transitive deps stay inside the existing allow-list (op-service/op-core/op-node/op-alt-da).

topPRs.title: chore(op-program): move cross package out of op-supervisor
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Relocates `op-supervisor/supervisor/backend/cross` to `op-program/client/interop/cross`. The package implements cross-chain hazard/cycle safety checks; its consumers are op-program's interop consolidation (`consolidate.go`, `interop_test.go`) and op-supervisor's backend workers — only op-program remains once op-supervisor is deleted.

Pure relocation — import paths rewritten in the 3 external consumers (op-program ×2, op-supervisor backend ×1). No logic changes.

Step toward deleting op-supervisor: with this and #20993 landed, the only remaining external imports of op-supervisor are the transitive deps the moved `cross` package pulls in (`op-supervisor/supervisor/{backend/reads,backend/superevents,types}`). Those go away with op-supervisor itself.
